name: Catalyst Turnaround
description: Korea-listed companies with an identifiable event that would repair the business and its balance sheet, held for as long as the event's own window and no longer. Keeps a catalyst ledger — scheduled, in progress, realised, delayed, failed — and never records a rising share price as a catalyst that worked.

managers.name: Catalyst Turnaround
managers.description: Finds Korea-listed companies where a named, sourced event would restore the business and its finances, writes the recovery path down to the cash-flow line, and manages the position by whether that event realises, slips or fails.

capabilities.reason: The book is what says whether this name is already held, at what weight, and how much of the account's single-name allowance other managers have taken. Sizing without it would be a per-strategy limit pretending to be an account limit.
A held position's invalidation conditions were written when it was opened, and a review that cannot read them is free to invent gentler ones after the fact.
Every catalyst row cites the evidence ids the reading was filed under, and a run has to be able to re-read what a previous run registered rather than re-fetching and re-deciding.

The catalyst register — which catalysts are open, how many times each has slipped, and which contrary findings are on the record — is this manager's own durable state and carries no copied vendor data.
A delay count that is not written back is a delay count that resets, and the rule against holding indefinitely through repeated delays is exactly the rule that needs the record to survive the run.

Filings and public policy documents: the receivable balance, the working-capital lines, the debt maturity schedule and the regulator's own notices are where a catalyst and its confirming indicator are actually read.
Adjusted won price history, for two numbers only — the distance to the price invalidation, which sizes the position, and the progress toward the target, which trims it.
